LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 5 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we organise ideas in our compositions? 2. How can you make your writing interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify the parts of a narrative composition,

2. work with peers to plan a narrative composition of about 160-200 words,

3. read sample narrative compositions with peers and critique them for: - correctness of language - flow or organisation of ideas - relevance to the topic - creativity

4. use the steps of the writing process to create a narrative composition of about (160 - 200 words), on tourist attraction sites,

5. use appropriate fixed phrases such as: catch fire; 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify the parts of a narrative composition,
2. work with peers to plan a narrative composition of about 160-200 words,
3. read sample narrative compositions with peers and critique them for: - correctness of language - flow or organisation of ideas - relevance to the topic - creativity
4. use the steps of the writing process to create a narrative composition of about (160 - 200 words), on tourist attraction sites,
5. use appropriate fixed phrases such as: catch fire; 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to communicate effectively is developed as they practise the skills of

writing clearly by following the stages of the writing process and creating a narrative composition.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s artistic skills are enhanced as they create and write narrative

compositions.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is displayed as the learner collaborates with peers to plan a narrative composition.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: The learner interacts with information on tourist attraction sites when creating a narrative

composition using the steps of the writing process thereby grasping knowledge on the environment.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of the writing process to their learning in Kiswahili.
